title: Soft-bodied organisms and remains on non-depositing sea floor are not preserved

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Soft-bodied organisms and remains on non-depositing sea floor are not preserved

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Wholly soft-bodied organisms are not preserved as fossils, and shells and bones decay and disappear where they lie on parts of the sea floor where sediment is not accumulating, so the fossil record is strongly biased.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. IX: On the Imperfection of the Geological Record

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: No organism wholly soft can be preserved. Shells and bones will decay and disappear when left on the bottom of the sea, where sediment is not accumulating.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter IX, “On the Imperfection of the Geological Record”; section “On the poorness of our palæontological collections”. Scope: fossil preservation of marine and other organisms

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch09-04: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.86

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Soft-bodied fossil occurrences and taphonomic associations are directly documented in public data. The absolute non-preservation statement is readily falsifiable and the broader bias can be quantified.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare preservation frequencies by tissue mineralization and depositional regime, and test for wholly soft-bodied fossils and skeletal remains in condensed or nondepositional settings. Verified soft-bodied fossils directly refute the absolute first clause, while taphonomic patterns test the bias.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Open fossil and living-marine databases contain the taxa, preservation modes, and environments needed to test both the absolute wording and the bias. A small team can cross-tabulate soft-bodied groups against fossil occurrences with standard joins. The absolute claim and the bias claim can come apart, and that split is itself a decisive outcome rather than a confound that blocks the test.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare the fossil record of wholly soft-bodied living phyla with that of biomineralizing taxa, and compare shell and bone preservation with sedimentation rate and depth. Any well-documented soft-bodied fossil refutes the absolute bar on preservation; a large deficit of soft-bodied taxa, and loss of shells where sediment does not accumulate, supports the bias claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Deep-sea living faunas and non-depositional seafloors are still unevenly sampled.

Exceptional preservation and secondary mineral films mean 'wholly soft' is not a single taphonomic class.

fields.label: Hypothesis
fields.value: Clause 1 (absolute): wholly soft-bodied organisms leave no fossils, so animal phyla without mineralised or sclerotised hard parts should have zero fossil occurrences. Clause 2 (bias): the fossil record is strongly biased toward organisms with hard parts, so fossil occurrences per living species should be far higher for biomineralising phyla than for wholly soft-bodied phyla.

fields.label: Method
fields.value: For each of 13 pre-registered wholly soft-bodied phyla and 6 biomineralising phyla, the phylum-level taxon was resolved in PBDB (taxa/list match_name, keeping accepted phylum-rank records so that homonyms such as the sloth clade 'Tardigrada' and the crane-fly genus 'Ctenophora' are excluded) and body-fossil occurrences counted with occs/list?base_id=...&pres=regular&rowcount. Accepted species per phylum were counted in the GBIF Backbone (species/search, status ACCEPTED), and living species estimated as total minus species flagged extinct. Occurrences per living species were compared between the two groups by medians; five example occurrences per soft-bodied phylum were saved to derived/soft_bodied_examples.csv.

fields.label: Pass criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered. Wholly soft-bodied phyla: Ctenophora, Platyhelminthes, Nemertea, Chaetognatha, Priapulida, Onychophora, Nematoda, Nematomorpha, Xenacoelomorpha, Gastrotricha, Placozoa, Rotifera, Tardigrada. Biomineralising phyla: Mollusca, Brachiopoda, Echinodermata, Bryozoa, Porifera, Cnidaria. For each phylum, count fossil occurrences in the Paleobiology Database (occs/list, rowcount) and accepted living species in the GBIF backbone taxonomy. Clause 1 is REFUTED if the soft-bodied phyla together have >= 10 fossil occurrences spread over >= 3 phyla, and SUPPORTED if they have 0. Clause 2 is SUPPORTED if the median of (fossil occurrences / living accepted species) over biomineralising phyla is >= 100 times the median over soft-bodied phyla, and REFUTED if it is < 10 times. Overall verdict: 'supports' if clause 1 supported and clause 2 supported; 'mixed' if clause 1 refuted and clause 2 supported; 'refutes' if clause 2 refuted (whatever clause 1 shows).

fields.label: Fail criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered. See pass_criterion: clause 1 fails on >= 10 occurrences in >= 3 soft-bodied phyla; clause 2 fails if the biomineralising/soft-bodied ratio of occurrences per living species is < 10. The third sentence of the claim (shells and bones decay where sediment is not accumulating) is not tested here; no public dataset pairs preservation with sedimentation rate at the needed scale, and the two assessors' operationalisations also concentrate on the first two clauses.

fields.label: Unit
fields.value: PBDB body-fossil occurrences in the 13 wholly soft-bodied phyla

fields.label: Interpretation
fields.value: Darwin's 'organism wholly soft' is read as membership of an animal phylum whose members have neither biomineralised skeletons nor robust sclerotised cuticles, jaws or tubes (list fixed above; Annelida, Hemichordata, Arthropoda and Chordata are excluded as mixed). 'Preserved' is read as having at least one occurrence recorded in the Paleobiology Database, which records body and trace fossils by taxon; trace fossils are excluded by restricting to body fossils where the API allows (pres=regular). The bias clause is read as the ratio of fossil occurrences to living described species, a crude but standard measure of preservation potential. Modern reinterpretation: the phylum-level classification and the notion of exceptional (Lagerstätte) preservation post-date Darwin.

fields.label: Datasets
fields.value:
Paleobiology Database, data service 1.2: occs/list record counts per phylum (body fossils)

GBIF Backbone Taxonomy, accepted species counts per phylum (species/search)

fields.label: Caveats
fields.value:
Clause 1 (absolute) is refuted: 937 body-fossil occurrences are recorded for 12 of the 13 soft-bodied phyla, including unambiguous ones such as ctenophores (Chengjiang, Hunsrück), nematodes and nematomorphs in amber, nemerteans (Solnhofen) and rotifers (Dominican amber). Even excluding phyla whose fossils are mostly sclerites or spines (Priapulida incl. palaeoscolecids, Chaetognatha incl. protoconodonts, Onychophora incl. Microdictyon plates), 184 occurrences remain in 9 phyla.

Clause 2 (bias) is strongly supported: the median mineralised phylum has 4.6 fossil occurrences per living species, the median soft-bodied phylum 0.005 (ratio ~960; pooled ratio 6.1 vs 0.017). Brachiopoda alone (316 per living species) reflect their far greater past diversity, not only preservation.

GBIF Backbone extinct flags are incomplete, so 'living species' (total minus flagged extinct) overestimates living diversity for groups with many unflagged fossil species (Mollusca), which makes the mineralised ratios conservative.

Some PBDB identifications of soft-bodied fossils are contested (e.g. the single 'Placozoa' and two 'Xenacoelomorpha' records from the Triassic of Troistedt); the clause-1 refutation does not depend on them.

The third clause of the claim (decay of shells and bones on non-depositing sea floor) was not tested; it would need taphonomic field data paired with sedimentation rates.
